name: goja-runtime-string-resource-budgets
instr:
goja cannot currently limit memory attributable to JavaScript strings per Runtime. Add an opt-in limit with configuration and usage exposed through a stable public API. Enforce it for host imports, compiled literals, built-in string operations, JSON, and regular expressions without changing JavaScript text. Unbudgeted Runtimes retain existing values, exceptions, lazy behavior, and reusability.

Make storage admission atomic. No operation may return, publish, or partially install a result unless retained and transient storage fits; failures restore prior accounting. Every string representation accounts its actual owned or retained storage exactly once in observable snapshots across creation, concatenation, and slicing: ASCII uses byte-backed storage, UTF-16 uses code-unit storage without altering lone surrogates, and cross-representation operations preserve identical JavaScript text while transferring charges without leaks or duplication. Reconcile lazy Go strings once when scanning selects a representation, leaving no transient residue. Balance transient usage after success, rejection, or callback panic. Reusable Programs use the executing Runtime's budget without shared accounting or contamination after rejection. Runtime.Set and Runtime.ToValue must reject excessive host strings before replacement or exposure. StringBudgetError reports Limit, Used, and Requested byte counts. Installing, replacing, disabling, or inspecting a budget preserves committed usage. Rejection leaves
